summary:
Team Leo Space built 'Still Out There', a virtual museum where visitors walk up to five 3D space artifacts and hear each one tell its story. The project addresses NASA Space Apps’ *Abandoned but not Forgotten* challenge by connecting equipment on the Moon, Mars, and in interstellar space to the discoveries it made possible.

Visitors can simulate bouncing a laser pulse off the Apollo 11 reflector to estimate the Moon’s distance, examine the mineral grains that helped Opportunity find evidence of past water on Mars, and listen to Voyager 1’s plasma-wave data as audio. The exhibits draw on NASA mission records, archival images, and 3D models. Narration and captions support exploration on computers and phones.

The museum helps young learners see how scientists use measurements to make discoveries and why a mission’s data can remain valuable for decades.
details:
What we built

Still Out There is a browser-based, first-person museum developed by Team Leo Space for NASA Space Apps’ Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Visitors explore five exhibits: the Apollo 11 retroreflector, Apollo 17 lunar rover, Opportunity rover, InSight lander, and Voyager 1. Walking up to an artifact starts its narrated story and timed captions. Visitors can replay the audio, read the full story, or use the exhibit directory to jump straight to an artifact. Approaching the exit starts a game-style credit roll with project references and team credits.

How it teaches

Each artifact tells its story in the first person and explains what it did and what scientists learned from it. Visitors can simulate a lunar laser-ranging experiment, inspect an image of the mineral grains Opportunity found on Mars, and listen to Voyager 1’s plasma-wave measurements as audio. These activities help young learners connect a piece of hardware to a measurement and understand how that measurement supported a scientific discovery.

How we built it

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js and WebGL for first-person movement and 3D rendering. We reconstructed the two Apollo exhibits from archival photographs and adapted NASA’s 3D models for Opportunity, InSight, and Voyager. We generated the narration using Kokoro Heart and paired the audio with timed captions. We used Vite to build the site, GitHub for version control, and Vercel for hosting.

What we considered

We designed the museum for keyboard and mouse on computers and touchscreen controls on phones. An opening guide explains how to move and look around. We optimized the models for browser loading and provided a CSS-based gallery for devices without WebGL. Full transcripts give visitors a way to follow each story at their own pace. We also credited the mission records, images, models, and recordings so visitors can explore the original sources.

Our intended impact is to help school-age learners understand how space science works and why the evidence a mission collects can keep teaching us long after the mission ends.
dataRefs: Voyager Captures Sounds of Interstellar Space
